COG.note: Systems named but not stated to be in use across government.

facts.fact: The French Treasury sheet says Congo's cybersecurity law and its law against cybercrime have been in force since June 2020.
The French Treasury sheet lists law no. 29 of 10 October 2019 on personal data protection among the laws reinforcing the sector's framework.
facts.system: Law no. 29 of 10/10/2019 on personal data protection

facts.fact: The universal access fund FASUCE, operational since 2020, has connected over 33,000 citizens in more than 173 localities and installed 183 mobile network sites, the Treasury sheet says.
Congo launched the World Bank-financed PATN in 2023 ($100 million), aimed at broadband access for underserved populations.
The French Treasury sheet lists law no. 37 of 12 December 2019 on electronic transactions among the laws reinforcing the sector's framework.
facts.system: Law no. 37 of 12/12/2019 on electronic transactions

facts.fact: The Treasury sheet says the PCN deployed about 3,000 km of fibre linking Pointe-Noire, Dolisie, Brazzaville, Oyo and Ouesso, operated and marketed by Congo Telecom, plus a 1,100 km secondary E2C network.

COG.note: No government payments to people stated.

facts.fact: The Treasury sheet says Congo has been on the WACS cable since May 2012 (landing at Matombi) and connected to the 2Africa cable since August 2023.

COG.note: No standards body membership or adoption stated.

facts.fact: The Treasury sheet says the tax system E-TAX was built in-house by the ministry's information systems directorate.

systems.country_label: 103% of population in subscriptions, October 2023 (5.8 million)

COG.note: Only subscription counts, not phone ownership.
No survey of account holding stated.

facts.fact: Under the World Bank-financed Central African Backbone, Congo has been interconnected to Gabon since 2018, operated commercially since 2019 by Mambs Services, the Treasury sheet says.
The Treasury sheet says Congo has been connected to Cameroon through the CAB project since 2022.
The Treasury sheet says Congo Telecom's underwater river cable has linked Brazzaville to Kinshasa in the DRC since 2017.
The Treasury sheet, citing ARPCE, says Mobile Money transactions in Congo reached over 238 billion FCFA in January 2024, across more than 79 million transactions.
The Treasury sheet says transactional platforms built with the mobile operators allow paperless payment of utility bills and, most recently, of land transport taxes.
The Treasury sheet lists law no. 71 of 16 August 2022 granting the digital start-up and technological innovation label.
The Treasury sheet names E-TAX, a tax and duties management system built in-house by the finance ministry, among reforms launched to collect revenue better.
